title: Affine splitting of the lci conormal transitivity sequence
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z$ be an affine scheme, and let $Z\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}X$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $u$ and $v$ are formally unramified, with the square-zero test definition of [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal]. Assume $u$ is a local complete intersection morphism: on compatible etale scheme charts it locally factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with the immersion ideal generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Use the conormal sheaves of the universal first-order thickenings [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal] and module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\mathcal C_{Z/Y}$ is finite locally free: locally on $Z$ it is a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_Z$, with rank allowed to vary. The canonical transitivity sequence of quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]
$$0\longrightarrow u^*\mathcal C_{Y/X}\xrightarrow{\lambda}\mathcal C_{Z/X}\xrightarrow{\rho}\mathcal C_{Z/Y}\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact and admits an $\mathcal O_Z$-linear section $s$ of $\rho$. Thus $(\lambda,s):u^*\mathcal C_{Y/X}\oplus\mathcal C_{Z/Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ is an isomorphism with the specified canonical first summand. Here $u^*$ is the module tensor pullback on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. The arrow $\lambda$ is induced by the morphism between the universal thickenings of $Z$ and $Y$ over $X$ extending $u$; for a closed immersion $v$ it is the map from the pulled-back ideal of $Y$ in $X$ modulo its square. The arrow $\rho$ is the conormal quotient for the composite $vu$.

source.place: Tags 06CB (lemma-unramified-lci), 06CC (lemma-transitivity-conormal-lci); criteria.tex proof of lemma-lci-unobstructed, first paragraph, for splitting on affine Z.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-unramified-lci-koszul-etale-charts] to $u$. Obtain an etale covering $p_a:W_a\to Z$ with $W_a\hookrightarrow V_a$ a closed immersion of affine schemes cut out by a finite Koszul-regular sequence, and $V_a\to Y$ etale. By [lem-sfb-universal-conormal-chart-transitivity], the restrictions of all three conormals and both transitivity maps are those for $W_a\hookrightarrow V_a\to X$; in particular $V_a\to X$ is still formally unramified. The closed-immersion identification of [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal] and the basis theorem [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] show that $p_a^*\mathcal C_{Z/Y}$ is finite free on each such chart. Thus [lem-sfb-etale-finite-free-zariski-descent] makes $\mathcal C_{Z/Y}$ Zariski finite locally free on $Z$, with variable rank.

source.place: Tags 06CB and 060D; the closed-immersion chart version uses 06C5/04HH and more-algebra.tex 062I.

proof.text: Fix one chart $W\hookrightarrow V\to X$. Let $V^+$ be the universal first-order thickening of $V$ over $X$ supplied by [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal]. Choose an affine etale scheme atlas $B_b\to V^+$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its pullbacks $V_b=V\times_{V^+}B_b$ and $W_b=W\times_VV_b$ are affine schemes, being closed subschemes of the affine $B_b$; closed immersions are representable by definition. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] these give etale coverings of $V$ and $W$. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-unramified-lci-koszul-etale-charts] keeps $W_b\hookrightarrow V_b$ Koszul regular. Shrink by standard opens of $B_b$ to obtain a finite Koszul-regular generating sequence on each $V_b$. By [lem-sfb-universal-conormal-chart-transitivity], $B_b$ is the universal thickening of $V_b$ over $X$: the explicit etale-lift clause applies to $V_b=V\times_{V^+}B_b$ and the etale map $B_b\to V^+$. Renaming this refined chart $W\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow V^+$, write $V^+=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$, where $I\subseteq J$, $I^2=0$, and $J/I$ has the stated Koszul-regular generators.

source.place: Tag 060D (lemma-universal-thickening-localize); affine scheme atlases of the universal thickening avoid any global schematicness theorem.

proof.text:
The universal thickening of $W$ over $X$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J^2)$. Indeed any test $T\hookrightarrow T'$ with an $X$-map $T\to W$ has a unique map $T'\to V^+$ extending $T\to V$. The ideal $J$ maps into the square-zero ideal of $T$ in $T'$, so $J^2$ maps to zero; this gives the unique factorization through $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J^2)$. This construction also works for algebraic-space tests, by the same ideal-sheaf argument. The universal properties in [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal] therefore identify the conormals on $W$ as
$$u_W^*\mathcal C_{V/X}=I/IJ,\qquad \mathcal C_{W/X}=J/J^2,\qquad \mathcal C_{W/V}=J/(I+J^2).$$
Here these are the small-etale modules associated to the displayed $A/J$-modules: tensor pullback along $W\to V$ of the module associated to $I$ is the module associated to $(A/J)\otimes_{A/I}I$ by the pullback comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], and $(A/J)\otimes_{A/I}I=I/JI$, using $I^2=0$; the last is $(J/I)/(J/I)^2$. The canonical first map sends $i\bmod IJ$ to $i\bmod J^2$, and the second is the quotient map. These are the ideal maps of the universal thickenings, so are the maps of [lem-sfb-universal-conormal-chart-transitivity].

source.place: Tag 06BF (lemma-transitivity-conormal-unramified), written on the affine universal thickening rather than suppressing its ideal calculation.

proof.text: Koszul regularity of the generators of $J/I$ implies $H_1$-regularity by the definition in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Hence [lem-sfb-h1-regular-quotient-ideal-intersection] gives $I\cap J^2=IJ$. The kernel of the first map in Step 3 is exactly $(I\cap J^2)/IJ=0$. The image is $(I+J^2)/J^2$, the kernel of the quotient onto $J/(I+J^2)$, and that quotient is surjective. Thus the sequence of $A/J$-modules is short exact, and the exact functor of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] makes the canonical sequence of associated small-etale modules short exact on each chart. Exactness of module sheaves is local for a covering: a section in a kernel locally lifts to the preceding term on these charts, and vanishing of a section is detected on the cover. This proves short exactness on $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0666 (lemma-conormal-sequence-H1-regular), the ideal calculation in divisors.tex Tag 063N and its use in spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 06CC.

proof.text: Put $K=u^*\mathcal C_{Y/X}$, $E=\mathcal C_{Z/X}$, $Q=\mathcal C_{Z/Y}$. The last two are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-universal-conormal], and $K$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Pass to their Zariski modules with [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]; the sequence is still short exact: the exact fully faithful functor of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] reflects exactness. Indeed its source kernels and cokernels are quasi-coherent, and exactness plus faithfulness detects the zero kernel/image quotient. Choose $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$. Since both $K$ and $Q$ are quasi-coherent, [lem-pc-affine-extension-section-surjectivity] makes $\Gamma(E)\to\Gamma(Q)$ surjective. Step 1 and [lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective] make $P=\Gamma(Q)$ projective over $R$. By the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], lift $\mathrm{id}_P$ through this surjection to an $R$-linear $t:P\to\Gamma(E)$ with $\Gamma(\rho)t=\mathrm{id}_P$.

source.place: Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed), first paragraph, expanded via schemes.tex Tag 01IE and algebra.tex Tag 05CE/05CF.

proof.text: The counit isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] turn $\widetilde t$ into $s:Q\to E$. Naturality of those counits gives $\rho s=\mathrm{id}_Q$, since $\Gamma(\rho)t=\mathrm{id}_P$. Carry $s$ back to the small etale site using the full faithful equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]; its identity-on-open-sections normalization keeps the same $\rho$ and hence the same section equation.

source.place: Tags 01I7/01IA/01IB, functoriality of the affine module correspondence; descent.tex 03DX.

proof.text: Define $\Phi:K\oplus Q\to E$ by $\Phi(k,q)=\lambda(k)+s(q)$. Locally a section $e$ satisfies $\rho(e-s\rho(e))=0$, so exactness gives a unique $k$ with $\lambda(k)=e-s\rho(e)$; uniqueness uses monicity of $\lambda$. These local $k$ agree on overlaps and define an $\mathcal O_Z$-linear map $r:E\to K$. The two formulas $r\lambda=\mathrm{id}$, $rs=0$ and $\lambda r+s\rho=\mathrm{id}$ show that $(r,\rho)$ is inverse to $\Phi$. In particular its first summand is exactly the specified canonical $\lambda$. Zero rank and empty schemes require no exception.

source.place: Tag 06D8 (lemma-lci-unobstructed), displayed chosen direct sum, with the elementary inverse formula written out.
